- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-period, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–1.5% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.7); apply +0.5% bias to forecast mean.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +1% daily), model often fails to capture continuation; extend upward bias by 0.5–1% for next 3 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to lag behind true price; add 0.5–1% lag correction to forecast for next 5 days.
